scope: 50 proposed fictional U.S. state Hitman chapter leaders and small crews; not live user accounts or geopolitical claims

national_hierarchy.established_hitman_immediate_cast_role: national story characters and specialist ensemble; do not force their locations into states
national_hierarchy.federal_district: District of Columbia is national council location only, no 51st state captain
national_hierarchy.protagonist_exception: McCluster is a PRIM-side Wildcard, NOT assigned as a Hitman state leader

political_reference.definition: Statewide presidential election winner; not gubernatorial or legislative party control
political_reference.maine_nebraska: Classified by statewide winner despite split district electoral votes
political_reference.disclaimer: The red/blue fiction mapping is a storytelling convention, NOT a factual statement linking real political parties, voters, states or demographic groups to crime.

chapter_structure.red: More mature organized fictional syndicates: legacy charter councils, inherited rank and long-standing compacts
chapter_structure.blue: Still-developing fictional street coalitions: younger neighborhood crews, fluid coalitions and cultural influence
chapter_structure.contested: States with competitive election histories may include rival factions and unstable succession; fiction only
chapter_structure.crews: Each state leader commands a 4–7-person fictional ensemble, including themselves. Supporting slots are templates, not added named recurring canon characters.
chapter_structure.rivalries: Curated, fictional interstate narrative tension; no real criminal network or street operation implied

global_prohibitions: No claims of real criminal affiliation
No real politicians as fictional gang members
No invented live account metrics, followers or endorsements
No active Core agent runner or social publisher
